solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: County towns ultimately chasing personnel

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the picked letter goes behind the workers piece

parts.note: personnel are the employees of an organisation

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word towns

explanation.surface: County towns end up pursuing employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts the S from towns after STAFF; Staffs is the short name for Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs is the standard abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county in the Midlands.

clue.text: Advise dim entrepreneur holding deposit

indicators.note: holding says the phrase contains the letters of the answer within it

explanation.surface: A recommendation to a slow-witted businessman about a deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the answer sits inside adviSE DIM ENTrepreneur; 'deposit' looks like a bank payment but means settled matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter laid down at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit in the geological sense.

clue.text: Ingenuous, with no feelings for a cockney

indicators.note: London cockney speech famously drops the initial H, so the word is said the cockney way

parts.note: someone with no feelings is heartless

explanation.surface: Someone innocent and unfeeling is mentioned in connection with a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner; said without its H, HEARTLESS sounds like ARTLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone simple and without guile, naive in a guileless way.

clue.text: Sample teas varying in strength

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the word for strength

parts.note: a forte is a person's strong point

indicators.note: varying shows the letters of teas are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tasting of teas of different strengths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sample teas' reads like a tasting, but 'Sample' alone is the definition; 'varying' makes ETAS from teas, which 'in' sets inside the strength word.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample or preview of something to come.

clue.text: Vulnerable zone wiped out after removing leader

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
removing leader means the first letter of zone is dropped

explanation.surface: A defenceless area is erased after its chief is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing leader' leaves ONE from ZONE; 'out' rearranges ONE plus WIPED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide open is fully exposed and so liable to attack or harm.

clue.text: Promiscuous daughter is put in frame

indicators.note: put in places the daughter and is pieces inside the word for frame

parts.note: to frame someone is to incriminate them with false evidence
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl with loose morals is set up for a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: To frame someone is to incriminate them falsely; DIS goes in after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Promiscuous in its older sense means unselective, mixing anything without discrimination.

clue.text: Proclaim one-time fortune turning up

parts.note: a one-time partner is an ex, a former one

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A former fortune emerging is being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' suits a down clue, where the fortune word is read upwards; 'one-time' is the usual crossword route to EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise loudly and publicly, to proclaim the merits of something.

clue.text: Edge up on serious traveller

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
up in a down clue reverses the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a lip is the edge or rim of a vessel
grim means stern or serious

explanation.surface: Someone sidles towards a solemn wayfarer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge up' looks like creeping forward, but 'up' reverses the edge word in this down clue, and 'on' sets it above the serious word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a person who journeys, typically to a sacred place.

clue.text: Niece loses heart — that's a relief for her brother

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letters of niece go, keeping only its ends

parts.note: phew is the exclamation uttered when relieved

explanation.surface: A niece is dispirited, and her sibling breathes out in relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip ICE from the middle of NIECE to leave NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece's brother is the son of the same sibling, so he is likewise a nephew to that aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Obstinate bunch come both unprotected and hopeful

indicators.note: both unprotected means each of the two words loses its outside letters

parts.note: a promising prospect is a hopeful one

explanation.surface: A stubborn group arrives, exposed yet optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNCH without its ends is UNC; COME without its ends is OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncompromising refuses to give ground, which is what obstinate means.

clue.text: End without a king — one died, with authority usurped

indicators.note: without means the a is taken out of the word for end

parts.note: death is the end of life
R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written
d is the standard abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A monarch's end: without a ruler, one is dead and power seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the A from the end word, giving DETH; R for king is from Latin rex, and the definition is the final phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dethroned ruler has been deposed, so the power once held has been taken over by others.

clue.text: Perennial insolence by trade union

indicators.note: by means placed beside, here the union piece comes first

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk or insolence

explanation.surface: A labour organisation gives backchat that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial' looks like an adjective meaning lasting; here it is a noun for a plant that returns each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a bulb plant that flowers year after year, so it is an example of a perennial.

clue.text: Set store by mother becoming expert

indicators.note: by puts the two pieces side by side, mother first

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters of store are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A mother valued highly turns into a master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set store by' reads as the idiom for valuing; 'Set' is the anagram signal turning STORE into ESTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially a distinguished musician, so an expert.

clue.text: Desire to follow Scottish Premier League's extravagant cash spending

indicators.note: to follow puts the desire piece after the league abbreviation

parts.note: SPL was the abbreviation for the Scottish Premier League in football
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A craving pursued by Scottish football's top division leads to lavish outlay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scottish Premier League was Scotland's top football division until 2013.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money lavishly, so a splurge is a spree of extravagant spending.

clue.text: They shouldn't be picked for front parts of aircraft

definitions.meaning: a humorous take on facial features one is told not to pick
the pointed forward ends of planes are called by the same word as facial features

explanation.surface: Parts of planes that ought not to be selected.
explanation.definitionFit: The facial organ and an aircraft's foremost section share the same name, as both lead from the front.

clue.text: Leave M protected by Bond, not fully committed

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart

indicators.note: protected by means the letter is enclosed within the bond word

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link
taken as written

explanation.surface: M, the spy chief, departs under Bond's protection, though only half-heartedly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes James Bond and his boss M; here Bond simply means TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Part-time work is done for only some of the hours, so the worker is not fully committed.

clue.text: Passing tennis shot, following return of skill

indicators.note: following places the shuffled letters after the reversed piece
return of means the word for skill is turned backwards

parts.note: art is skill or craft

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the letters of tennis are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passing shot in tennis follows a skilful return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' and 'tennis shot' look like one phrase, a passing shot; 'Passing' is the definition. ART reversed is TRA; 'shot' rearranges TENNIS into NSIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient lasts only briefly, it is passing.

clue.text: Hide from onset of this during terrible soaking

indicators.note: during means the letter sits within the reworked letters
terrible signals the letters of soaking are in a mess and rearranged
onset of picks the first letter of this

explanation.surface: Taking shelter from the start of a dreadful drenching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, take cover; it is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatskin is the skin of a goat, a hide in the leather sense.

clue.text: Parasite struggling war poet married

indicators.note: struggling signals that the letters of war poet are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: A First World War poet, wed and in difficulty, is a hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges the war poet letters into TAPEWOR; the surface hints at a First World War poet, but no poet is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a flat worm living in the gut of its host, an example of a parasite.

clue.text: Girl with hat is a leech, for example

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a hat is said to be a bloodsucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leech' suggests a scrounging person; here it is the worm.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are segmented worms, and the leech belongs to that group.

clue.text: Trouble since accommodating King George

indicators.note: accommodating means holding the royal abbreviation inside

parts.note: ago means since or in the past, as in long ago
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Bother has followed ever since the king was put up.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British for aggressive behaviour or hassle, which is trouble.

clue.text: Reagan planned to seize diamonds from an island in the Caribbean

indicators.note: to seize means the rearranged letters take hold of the diamonds letter inside
planned signals that the letters of Reagan are arranged anew

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: President Reagan plotted to grab gems from a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 1983 US invasion of Grenada ordered by Reagan.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is an island nation in the southern Caribbean.

clue.text: Soak up the sailor's world!

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor, and the s comes with the possessive
an orb is a sphere or globe, so the world

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a seaman's world.
explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb is to take in or soak up liquid.

clue.text: Indonesian island welcoming English from Bangladesh

indicators.note: welcoming means the island takes in the English abbreviation

parts.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: An Indonesian island receives an Englishman from Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali describes the people and language of Bengal, which includes Bangladesh.

clue.text: Extra charge for university lecturer after a day

indicators.note: after places the lecturer piece behind the a and day pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A fee for an academic after a day's work.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is something extra attached, such as a supplementary charge on a bill.

clue.text: Developing source of arum in new perfume

indicators.note: in places the picked letter within the new and perfume pieces

parts.note: scent is perfume

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of arum

explanation.surface: A fresh fragrance draws on the essence of arum lilies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Ring shop selling food on the way back, drunk

parts.note: O is a ring because of its shape

indicators.note: on the way back means the shop word is read in reverse

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling food

explanation.surface: Someone phones a food shop while returning home tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call; it is the letter O. DELI reversed is ILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, as in well-oiled.

clue.text: The kid ran off without being told

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: The child ran away without being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges THE KID RAN; 'without being told' looks like part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed, unaware of the facts.

clue.text: Banter is sick when getting on!

parts.note: bad means ill or sick, as in feeling bad
in age means when advancing in years, getting on

explanation.surface: Someone jokes that being ill is part of growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD then IN AGE; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful repartee, another word for teasing chat.

clue.text: The end of chess coach's riddle

indicators.note: the end of takes the last letter of chess

parts.note: to train is to coach, the s being just possessive

explanation.surface: The final part of a chess coach's puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riddle' looks like a puzzle, but here it is a verb, to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle soil is to pass it through a sieve, which is to strain it.
